Tasks.Name: Passwordless / WHfB
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Windows Hello for Business (WHfB) is a core passwordless authentication technology for Windows devices and Cloud PCs. It replaces reusable passwords with device-bound credentials protected by the platform and unlocked by PIN, biometrics, or both. This makes phishing and credential replay materially harder than in password-based designs.

Windows Hello for Business (WHfB) delivers both a streamlined sign-in experience and strong, phishing-resistant authentication. Successful adoption depends on choosing the right trust model (cloud Kerberos trust), aligning Intune and Microsoft Entra ID policies, and communicating the registration flow clearly to end users.

## Implementation Guidance

1. Choose the trust model deliberately. For many modern environments, cloud trust is the preferred starting point because it simplifies deployment while still supporting passwordless sign-in. Key trust or certificate trust may still be required in some hybrid environments, but should be justified by documented dependencies.
2. Configure WHfB through Microsoft Intune using the supported Windows enrollment or identity policy path. Define PIN requirements, biometric use, anti-spoofing expectations where applicable, and whether the setup is mandatory for targeted users.
3. Align WHfB with Conditional Access and authentication-strength strategy in Microsoft Entra. For high-value apps and privileged roles, consider requiring stronger phishing-resistant methods where supported by your broader identity design.
4. Pilot with a representative group of users and hardware. Validate biometric enrollment, PIN fallback, recovery scenarios, shared-device implications, and remote or hybrid-work onboarding experiences before expanding tenant-wide.
5. Publish clear user guidance. Explain why the organization is moving to passwordless sign-in, what users will see during enrollment, how privacy works for biometrics, and how to recover if a device is replaced or reset.

Tasks.Name: MAM for Edge & Secure Enterprise Browser
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Microsoft Edge can be part of a data-protection strategy for unmanaged or lightly managed Windows devices by combining Intune app protection capabilities, app configuration, and Conditional Access controls. This is useful when the organization needs to protect browser-based access to Microsoft 365 or other web apps without fully enrolling every personal device.

For Zero Trust, the objective is to protect organizational data in the app, validate user and session conditions, and reduce copy, save, or exfiltration paths on endpoints that are not managed to the same standard as corporate devices.

## Implementation Guidance

### Define the BYOD and unmanaged access policy
- Decide which users or device populations are allowed browser-only access instead of full device enrollment, and document what data actions must be blocked or limited.
- Confirm the current Microsoft support matrix for Intune app protection on Windows and Microsoft Edge for Business before designing policy around it.
- Pair browser protection with Conditional Access policies that distinguish unmanaged, compliant, and corporate-owned devices.

### Configure protection controls
- Use Intune app configuration and supported app protection settings for Microsoft Edge to enforce organization-approved browser behavior where available.
- Configure Conditional Access so sensitive applications require either a compliant device or the approved protected browser path, depending on risk and business need.
- Test download controls, cut/copy/paste behavior, and sign-in continuity with representative SaaS apps before production rollout.

### Operate with clear guardrails
- Provide user guidance that explains the difference between full device management and browser-protected access on personal devices.
- Monitor sign-in and Conditional Access results to confirm users land in the intended access path instead of failing unexpectedly.
- Review whether high-risk roles should be moved from protected-browser access to fully managed devices over time.

Tasks.Name: PIN or Biometric
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Access requirements are the policy decisions that determine what a user and device must satisfy before reaching organizational resources. In the Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Entra ecosystem, that can mean requiring a compliant device, requiring an approved client app, requiring app protection policy, or combining those conditions with strong authentication and risk signals. In Zero Trust, the right access requirement depends on resource sensitivity and device ownership rather than a single one-size-fits-all rule.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Classify access scenarios first: internal users on corporate devices, BYOD mobile users, partners, frontline shared devices, and privileged administrators often need different requirements.
2. Require a compliant device for the highest-sensitivity workloads where the organization needs strong assurance of encryption, patching, health, and management state.
3. Use the **Require app protection policy** Conditional Access grant for supported mobile BYOD scenarios where full enrollment is not necessary or appropriate.
4. Align Conditional Access with the Intune policy model. A compliant-device requirement only works well when compliance policies are realistic, current, and monitored for exceptions.
5. Document exception paths and review them regularly. Long-lived access exceptions are one of the fastest ways to erode a Zero Trust design.
6. Test failure modes from the user point of view. Users and support staff should understand whether denial happened because of device compliance, app requirement, sign-in risk, or another control.

Tasks.Name: MAM Conditional Access
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
For mobile access, organizations often need to balance user productivity with data protection on devices they do not fully manage. Microsoft Intune app protection policies can protect data inside supported apps, while Microsoft Entra Conditional Access can require either a protected app experience or a compliant device depending on the resource and risk scenario.

Zero Trust requires that you choose the right control for the scenario instead of treating all mobile access the same.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Separate your access patterns into clear scenarios:
   - **BYOD / unmanaged**: require app protection policy and supported client apps.
   - **Corporate-owned or highly regulated**: require device compliance in addition to app protection where needed.
2. In Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, use current controls such as:
   - **Require app protection policy**
   - **Require approved client app** where still appropriate for the targeted cloud app and client platform
   - **Require device to be marked as compliant** for managed-device scenarios
3. Do not describe app protection users as "compliant devices" unless an actual Intune compliance policy is being evaluated.
4. Align Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Teams access rules so the user experience is consistent.
5. Test with pilot users on both Android and iOS/iPadOS, including scenarios where the user signs in from a non-protected app.
6. Document break-glass and exception handling for executives, contractors, and support accounts.
7. Review sign-in logs, Conditional Access insights, and Intune app protection reports to validate that the intended policy path is being used.

A strong design explains not only what to require, but why one population gets app protection while another must use an enrolled and compliant device.

Tasks.Name: Backup to Android backup services
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Data protection settings in Microsoft Intune app protection policies define how organizational data can move, be stored, and be used inside protected mobile apps. These controls are central to a Zero Trust mobile strategy because they create the boundary that keeps work data from flowing freely into unmanaged apps, storage locations, or services.

Administrators should treat these settings as a baseline standard, not as one-off exceptions per app.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Start with the primary data movement decisions:
   - Can users copy and paste work data to personal apps?
   - Can users save files to personal storage locations?
   - Can users open work documents in unmanaged apps?
   - Can users print or share work data outside protected apps?
2. Build a minimum baseline for all users that keeps organizational data within managed apps and approved services.
3. Increase restrictions for higher-risk groups, especially if they handle regulated or confidential information.
4. Test real user workflows such as opening attachments, saving annotated files, and moving between Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, and Edge.
5. Do not rely on a single setting. Combine data transfer restrictions, encryption, access requirements, Conditional Launch, and selective wipe.
6. Publish exception criteria so business units understand when a less restrictive policy is justified.
7. Review policy effectiveness with security, legal, and business stakeholders at least annually.

The best data protection design is one that blocks risky data movement while still allowing approved productivity paths.

Tasks.Name: Backup to iCloud
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
For iOS/iPadOS app protection scenarios, administrators should evaluate whether organizational data stored by protected apps can be included in consumer backup locations such as iCloud or local device backups. In Zero Trust terms, unmanaged backup destinations can create an additional copy of business data outside the app protection boundary.

The recommended posture for most organizations is to prevent protected app data from being backed up to consumer backup services unless there is a documented business requirement and compensating controls.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Identify which iOS/iPadOS apps store organization data locally and are managed through Intune app protection policies.
2. In the Microsoft Intune admin center, review the iOS/iPadOS app protection policy data protection settings that control backup of organization data.
3. For BYOD and lightly managed mobile scenarios, prefer the setting that prevents backup of work data to consumer backup locations.
4. Validate how Microsoft 365 mobile apps behave after device replacement or app reinstallation so support teams can explain the recovery experience to users.
5. Communicate clearly that blocking backup of work data does not prevent the user from backing up personal content; it limits protected organizational content.
6. If executives or regulated teams require stricter data handling, combine this setting with controls for save-as, copy/paste, print, screen capture, and approved apps.

This setting is usually most valuable where the device itself is not corporately managed, because app protection is acting as the primary control plane for organizational data.

Tasks.Name: Send org data to other apps
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Data protection in Microsoft Intune often starts with app protection policies that keep organizational data inside approved managed apps. Many organizations use a tiered model so they can apply a baseline set of controls broadly and reserve stricter settings for more sensitive roles or information types. In Zero Trust, this is a practical way to align data sensitivity with user impact instead of treating every app and every mobile workflow the same.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Define a small number of protection tiers, such as baseline, enhanced, and high protection, based on the sensitivity of the data and the risk profile of the users.
2. For the baseline tier, require core controls such as approved apps, work-data encryption in supported apps, and selective wipe capability.
3. For enhanced or high-protection tiers, consider stronger access requirements such as app PIN, biometrics, stricter data-transfer restrictions, shorter recheck intervals, or narrower save locations.
4. Map each tier to real user populations and business scenarios. Tier design should follow data sensitivity and risk, not generic labels.
5. Pilot with representative users before scaling. Data-protection settings that are technically correct can still fail if critical app workflows were not tested.
6. Review offboarding and incident-response flows so the organization can wipe work data quickly without unnecessary action on personal data.

## Overview
Data protection in Microsoft Intune often starts with app protection policies that keep organizational data inside approved managed apps. Many organizations use a tiered model so they can apply a baseline set of controls broadly and reserve stricter settings for more sensitive roles or information types. In Zero Trust, this is a practical way to align data sensitivity with user impact instead of treating every app and every mobile workflow the same.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Define a small number of protection tiers, such as baseline, enhanced, and high protection, based on the sensitivity of the data and the risk profile of the users.
2. For the baseline tier, require core controls such as approved apps, work-data encryption in supported apps, and selective wipe capability.
3. For enhanced or high-protection tiers, consider stronger access requirements such as app PIN, biometrics, stricter data-transfer restrictions, shorter recheck intervals, or narrower save locations.
4. Map each tier to real user populations and business scenarios. Tier design should follow data sensitivity and risk, not generic labels.
5. Pilot with representative users before scaling. Data-protection settings that are technically correct can still fail if critical app workflows were not tested.
6. Review offboarding and incident-response flows so the organization can wipe work data quickly without unnecessary action on personal data.

Tasks.Name: Screen Capture
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
On Android, organizations may need to reduce the risk that protected app content is exposed through screen capture, digital assistant surfaces, previews, or other convenience features that can relay sensitive data outside the managed app boundary. These settings are particularly relevant for users who handle confidential or regulated data on personally owned devices.

In Zero Trust, this is another way of limiting unintended disclosure paths even after the user has been authenticated.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Determine which user groups truly need restrictions on screenshots and assistant-style surfaces. Not every population requires the strictest setting.
2. In the Microsoft Intune admin center, review the Android app protection policy data protection settings related to screen capture and assistant exposure.
3. Apply stricter restrictions to high-sensitivity groups first, then evaluate broader rollout.
4. Test protected workflows such as viewing email, Teams chat content, and documents in supported apps.
5. Confirm whether the restriction affects legitimate support, accessibility, or training use cases.
6. Communicate clearly that the control is designed to protect organizational data, not to monitor personal use.

These controls are most valuable when combined with copy/paste, save-as, approved keyboard, and browser protections to create a coherent managed-app boundary.

Tasks.Name: App Condition
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Conditional Launch in Microsoft Intune app protection policies is used to decide what happens when a protected app no longer meets a required security condition. Instead of trusting the app session indefinitely, Intune can warn the user, block access, or wipe the organization account data from the app when conditions such as device integrity, app version, OS version, or offline duration fall out of policy.

For Zero Trust, this matters because access to organizational data should remain continuously evaluated. Conditional Launch helps enforce that principle even on personally owned devices that are not fully enrolled in Intune, as long as the app supports Intune app protection.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Start by identifying which users will use app protection without full device enrollment, such as BYOD mobile users.
2. In the Microsoft Intune admin center, create or update an app protection policy for Android and/or iOS/iPadOS.
3. Configure the **Conditional launch** section to evaluate conditions that materially affect data risk, such as:
   - Maximum offline grace period
   - Minimum app version
   - Minimum supported OS version
   - Rooted or jailbroken device detection
   - Threat signals when integrated with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint or another supported mobile threat defense partner
4. Prefer **Block access** before **Wipe data** for most conditions unless the risk is clearly high and your support process is ready.
5. Pair app protection policies with Microsoft Entra Conditional Access where appropriate, such as requiring an approved client app or app protection policy for Exchange Online and SharePoint Online.
6. Pilot with a small user group first. Verify user prompts, remediation messages, and selective wipe behavior before broad rollout.
7. Review Conditional Launch values at least quarterly so minimum versions and grace periods stay aligned to current support policy.

Good practice is to document which conditions are meant to protect confidentiality, which are meant to maintain app hygiene, and which trigger account-data wipe instead of a user-remediation flow.

Tasks.Name: Jailbroken/rooted devices
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Conditional Launch settings in Microsoft Intune app protection policies define what should happen when the app, device, or environment no longer meets security expectations. They are a continuous-control mechanism for app-protected data and are especially useful in BYOD and mobile app management-only scenarios.

This topic should focus on design decisions, not just enumerate settings.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Prioritize the conditions that create the biggest real-world risk in your environment:
   - Rooted or jailbroken device detection
   - Minimum operating system version
   - Minimum app version
   - Maximum offline grace period
   - Device integrity or threat posture signals where supported
2. For each condition, choose the response deliberately:
   - **Warn** when the user can reasonably remediate without immediate business interruption
   - **Block access** when the condition materially weakens security
   - **Wipe data** only when the risk is high enough to justify automatic removal of organizational account data from the app
3. Keep response choices consistent across similar user populations unless there is a documented reason to vary them.
4. Test policy outcomes on supported Android and iOS/iPadOS apps before production assignment.
5. Review minimum version values regularly so they do not become stale or impossible for users to satisfy.
6. Coordinate Conditional Launch with threat-defense tooling and Conditional Access so the device, app, and cloud layers reinforce one another.
7. Publish a remediation guide for users and support teams.

Conditional Launch should not be treated as a miscellaneous settings bucket. It is part of the organization’s ongoing access evaluation strategy.

Tasks.Name: Require Threat Scan on apps
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
The **Require threat scan on apps** setting for Android app protection policies uses Google Play Protect signals to help determine whether a device is in a safer state before protected work data is accessed. In a Zero Trust design, this is a lightweight but useful control for personally owned Android devices where the organization wants application-level protection without requiring full device enrollment.

This control should be treated as one signal, not a complete mobile threat defense strategy.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Use this setting only in an **Android app protection policy** scenario where the protected apps support Intune app protection.
2. Decide whether your organization should **warn** or **block access** when Google Play Protect app scanning is off. A warning is easier for pilot phases; blocking is stronger for production.
3. Scope the policy to users who access organizational data from personally owned Android devices or from MAM-only scenarios.
4. Pair this setting with other Android app protection controls such as PIN/biometric access, controlled data transfer, and restrictions on saving organizational data to personal storage.
5. Provide end-user instructions for turning Google Play Protect back on, because the most common failure case is simply that the device user disabled scanning.
6. Review reporting for potentially harmful apps and failed access attempts so you can see whether this setting is producing real security value or unnecessary friction.

Tasks.Name: Require Play Integrity Verdict
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Google replaced the legacy *SafetyNet Attestation API* with the **Google Play Integrity API**. In Microsoft Intune App Protection Policies (APP) and Android Compliance Policies, the **Play Integrity Verdict** setting verifies the integrity of Android devices before allowing access to corporate data.

### Important October 31, 2026 Enforcement Update
Google updated the definition of **Strong Integrity** (`MEETS_STRONG_INTEGRITY`) for devices running **Android 13 and later**, requiring both hardware-backed security signals and a **security update within the past 12 months**. Microsoft Intune enforces this updated definition starting **October 31, 2026**:
- Devices on Android 13+ without a security patch in the last 12 months are downgraded from *Strong Integrity* to *Device Integrity* (`MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY`), which can trigger conditional launch blocks or mark devices noncompliant.
- Admins should pair Play Integrity checks with the **Min OS version** and **Min patch version** conditional launch settings (and **Minimum security patch level** in MDM compliance policies) to warn users before they are blocked.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Configure the **Play Integrity verdict** conditional launch setting in your Android app protection policies (**Apps > App protection policies**) and Android Enterprise compliance policies.
2. Select the appropriate integrity tier (**Basic integrity**, **Device integrity**, or **Strong integrity**) based on user risk and device hardware capabilities.
3. Combine Play Integrity checks with **Min OS version**, **Min patch version**, **Min app version**, Mobile Threat Defense signals, and Microsoft Entra Conditional Access.
4. Pilot any integrity-based blocking with a representative Android device set, because OEM and Google-service dependencies can affect results.
5. Provide a support path for users whose devices fail integrity checks even though they believe the device is healthy.
6. Monitor Intune app protection status reports regularly to identify devices failing Play Integrity checks due to outdated security patches.

Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Samsung Knox attestation can provide an additional device-integrity signal for supported Samsung devices in Microsoft Intune app protection scenarios. It is intended to help determine whether a device is genuine and in a healthy enough state to be trusted with protected organizational data.

In Zero Trust, vendor-specific attestation should be treated as a supplemental signal, not the only trust decision.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Confirm that the target Android population actually includes supported Samsung devices and that the required Samsung/Intune prerequisites are in place.
2. Decide whether the control is being used for a Samsung-specific deployment, an executive/high-risk population, or a rugged/frontline scenario.
3. Configure the attestation-related app protection setting only for user/device populations where the check is meaningful.
4. Use assignment filters or separate policies if you need to scope the behavior specifically to Samsung devices.
5. Choose the response action carefully. In most cases, **Block access** is easier to support than immediate **Wipe data**.
6. Test the user experience, including terms acceptance and remediation steps.
7. Keep a fallback plan for non-Samsung devices so the security standard remains consistent across Android platforms.

Samsung-specific controls can be valuable for corporate Samsung fleets, but they should complement a broader Android device integrity strategy across all OEMs.

Tasks.Name: Mobile Threat Defense
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Mobile threat signals help organizations decide whether a device should be trusted to access organizational resources. In Microsoft Intune, threat data from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint or supported partner solutions can be incorporated into device compliance so that risky devices are blocked or remediated before they access Microsoft 365 and other protected apps.

This is a strong Zero Trust control because device trust is evaluated continuously, not assumed just because the device enrolled successfully once.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Choose the mobile threat signal source you will standardize on, such as **Microsoft Defender for Endpoint** or a supported partner.
2. Configure the relevant connector in the **Microsoft Intune admin center** and confirm the required licensing and administrator roles.
3. Deploy the mobile threat app or onboarding experience to the target platforms and ensure devices successfully report risk state.
4. Create or update **device compliance policies** so the device risk level must be at or below your accepted threshold.
5. Use **Conditional Access** to require a compliant device for access to Microsoft 365 and other sensitive services.
6. Define the operational process for false positives, incident triage, and user remediation so security and support teams know how devices return to compliance.
7. Periodically review which platforms and partner integrations are still supported, because the ecosystem changes over time.

Tasks.Name: Compliance policy
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Compliance policies are one of the most important device signals in a Zero Trust architecture. Microsoft Intune evaluates whether devices meet your required state, such as minimum OS version, encryption, password requirements, Secure Boot, Microsoft Defender health, or risk posture from integrated security tooling. Microsoft Entra Conditional Access can then use the resulting compliance signal to allow, limit, or block access to corporate resources.

## Implementation Guidance
- Define the minimum security controls per platform and per sensitivity tier. Typical starting points include encryption, OS minimum versions, Microsoft Defender status, device threat level, and jailbreak or root detection where applicable.
- Create separate compliance policies for major platform or ownership differences instead of forcing one policy to fit every device class.
- Configure actions for noncompliance intentionally, including grace periods, user notifications, and whether immediate access loss is appropriate for each policy breach.
- If licensed, integrate Microsoft Defender for Endpoint device risk signals so access decisions can reflect both configuration state and active threat posture.
- Use Conditional Access to require devices to be marked compliant for high-value apps and data, while preserving emergency or break-glass access paths for true business continuity scenarios.
- Review compliance reports regularly and tune policies when false positives, unsupported hardware, or business exceptions create unnecessary friction.

Tasks.Name: Conditional access policy
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Conditional Access in Microsoft Entra ID evaluates signals such as user, app, sign-in risk, device state, location, and authentication strength to determine whether access should be allowed, blocked, or subject to additional controls.
For device security workshops, the most important patterns are requiring a compliant device, requiring approved client apps or app protection on BYOD, and layering MFA or stronger authentication for sensitive access. Conditional Access is where Zero Trust policy becomes an actual gate.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Define the protected resources first: Microsoft 365, private web apps, admin portals, or selected cloud apps. Different resources often justify different device requirements.
2. Use a phased rollout. Build the policy in report-only mode first, review impact in sign-in logs and the Conditional Access insights workbook, then enforce after validation.
3. For corporate or enrolled-device scenarios, require the device to be marked as compliant. For BYOD app-only scenarios, consider controls such as approved client app or app protection policy instead of full device compliance.
4. Maintain emergency-access exclusions and document them carefully. Zero Trust requires resilience as well as restriction.
5. Avoid stacking unnecessary controls that create user friction without reducing real risk. Use the minimum set that enforces business and regulatory requirements.
6. Review policy results continuously after deployment, especially after major enrollment, app, or operating system changes.

Tasks.Name: Enrollment Restrictions
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Enrollment restrictions in Microsoft Intune help define which platforms, ownership models, and device volumes are allowed into management. In a Zero Trust program, they are part of the front door: they reduce accidental or unauthorized enrollment paths and help make sure devices use the organization's intended onboarding methods, such as Windows Autopilot, Apple Automated Device Enrollment, or Android Enterprise.

## Implementation Guidance
- Define which platforms and ownership scenarios your organization supports, and separate corporate-owned onboarding from personally owned or partner-managed cases.
- Use device platform restrictions to block unsupported platforms and outdated operating system versions from enrolling in Intune in the first place.
- Use device limit restrictions to prevent users from enrolling excessive numbers of devices, especially in shared-account or abuse scenarios.
- Align restrictions with documented enrollment paths such as Autopilot, Apple Automated Device Enrollment, Android Enterprise, and company-owned dedicated device scenarios.
- Create an exception process for legitimate edge cases such as lab devices or transitional migrations, rather than weakening the baseline for everyone.
- Communicate restriction behavior clearly to support teams and end users so blocks are expected and actionable rather than confusing.

## Reference

Tasks.Name: Mobile Threat Defense (MTD Role & Auto-Launch)
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

**Mobile Threat Defense (MTD)** solutions (such as **Microsoft Defender for Endpoint** or supported partners like Zimperium, Lookout, Check Point, Pradeo, **Trustd Mobile**, and **iVerify Enterprise**) integrate with Microsoft Intune to detect malware, phishing, network threats, OS vulnerabilities, and malicious certificates on iOS/iPadOS and Android devices, feeding real-time device risk signals into Intune Compliance and App Protection Policies.

Major 2026 enhancements eliminate common mobile MTD deployment gaps:
- **Grant MTD Role Permissions on Android COBO & COPE (June 2026 / 2605):** A new **Grant MTD role permissions** toggle on the Intune MTD connector page grants enhanced OS-level exemptions to your chosen MTD app on corporate-owned fully managed (COBO) and corporate-owned work profile (COPE) Android devices:
  - **Exempt from Suspension & Hibernation:** The OS cannot suspend or hibernate the MTD app.
  - **Exempt from Power Restrictions:** Can start foreground services from the background without battery optimization throttling.
  - **Protected from User Termination:** End users **cannot force-stop the app or clear its app data**, preventing users from disabling endpoint protection.
- **Automatically Launch Microsoft Defender for Endpoint During Android Setup (June/September 2026 / 2605 & 2609):** When enabled on the Defender for Endpoint connector page, Intune automatically opens Defender during out-of-box enrollment on Android COBO and COPE devices so initial onboarding completes during device setup without relying on the user to open the app manually.
- **Rooted Android Devices Blocked from Microsoft Tunnel (November 2025):** The Defender client on Android automatically detects root status, elevates device risk to *High*, and immediately drops and blocks Microsoft Tunnel VPN connections.
- **iOS Certificate Inventory Sync with Zimperium (February 2026 / 2601):** Synchronizes installed certificate inventory from managed iOS/iPadOS devices to detect malicious root/identity certificates.

## Implementation Guidance

1. Choose the mobile threat signal source deliberately. If you are standardizing on Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, document the mobile onboarding, privacy expectations, and supported platforms. If you use a partner integration, document where device risk is authored and where enforcement happens.
2. Integrate the signal with Intune compliance policies. Keep the compliance logic simple at first, such as requiring the device risk level to stay below an agreed threshold, then build exceptions only where justified.
3. Use Conditional Access to consume the compliance result instead of trying to duplicate risk logic across multiple places. Your goal is one policy path that administrators can explain and troubleshoot.
4. Pilot with clear help-desk messaging. Users need to know what happens if malware, a risky network, or device tampering causes access to be blocked, and how they can remediate the issue.
5. Review privacy and data collection notices with legal and HR as needed, especially in BYOD scenarios. Threat defense should focus on enterprise risk, not unnecessary collection of personal content.
6. Measure false positives and time to remediation. Security value drops quickly if users and administrators cannot tell why a device became noncompliant.

Tasks.Name: Certificates
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Certificate deployment with Microsoft Intune is commonly used to establish device trust for Wi-Fi, VPN, email, web authentication, and other Zero Trust controls. In a modern deployment, administrators typically use trusted certificate profiles together with SCEP, PKCS, PFX, or Microsoft Cloud PKI-based issuance so devices can automatically receive the certificates they need. The goal is to replace shared secrets and manual certificate handling with managed, revocable credentials tied to known devices and users.

## Implementation Guidance
- Decide which certificate use cases you are solving first: Wi-Fi and VPN client authentication, device authentication, secure email, app authentication, or certificate-based Conditional Access dependencies.
- Standardize the trust chain by deploying trusted root and intermediate certificates to the target Windows devices before you deploy client certificates.
- Choose the right issuance model: SCEP for large-scale automated issuance, PKCS where direct CA issuance is preferred, PFX only for specialized scenarios, and Microsoft Cloud PKI where it fits your licensing and architecture.
- If you use on-premises PKI, validate connector and NDES requirements, certificate templates, CRL reachability, renewal intervals, and high availability before broad deployment.
- Assign certificate profiles in pilot rings, then validate issuance, renewal, revocation behavior, and the downstream profiles that depend on the certificate, such as Wi-Fi or VPN.
- Document recovery procedures for expired or failed certificates, and monitor Intune, connector, and CA health so broken renewals do not silently disrupt access.

## Reference

- **[Use SCEP certificate profiles with Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-configuration/certificates/scep-profiles)** — Shows how to create and assign SCEP certificate profiles in Intune.
- **[Use a PKCS certificate profile to provision devices with certificates in Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-configuration/certificates/pkcs-profiles)** — Shows how to use PKCS certificate profiles to provision certificates to devices.

Tasks.Name: VPN
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
VPN profiles in Microsoft Intune let administrators deploy remote access settings consistently across managed devices. In a Zero Trust architecture, VPN should not be treated as blanket trust; instead, it should be scoped to specific applications, networks, or device scenarios and paired with strong authentication, compliant device requirements, and continuous monitoring. Intune helps standardize the client side of that design across Windows and other supported platforms.

## Implementation Guidance
- Choose the remote access pattern first: Windows built-in VPN, Always On VPN, partner VPN clients, or Microsoft Tunnel for supported mobile scenarios. Do not assume one profile type fits every platform.
- Prefer certificate-based authentication such as EAP-TLS where possible, and deploy the trusted root and client certificate chain before assigning the VPN profile.
- Define split-tunnel versus full-tunnel routing intentionally. Split tunneling often provides better user experience, but it requires clear DNS, proxy, and application access planning.
- Use Microsoft Entra Conditional Access and device compliance to control who can reach sensitive applications, rather than treating a VPN connection as full trust by itself.
- Pilot with a small set of users across home, hotel, cellular, and branch-office networks to validate DNS resolution, tunnel persistence, proxy interactions, and identity prompts.
- Monitor connection failures, certificate renewals, and tunnel health, and document support runbooks for expired certs, bad routes, and fallback access methods.

Tasks.Name: Wi-Fi
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Wi-Fi profiles in Microsoft Intune let administrators deploy consistent wireless settings to managed devices so users can connect securely without manually entering configuration details. In a Zero Trust program, Wi-Fi profiles matter because they can enforce stronger authentication methods, reduce reliance on shared passwords, and pair with certificate-based access so only approved users and devices join sensitive networks.

## Implementation Guidance
- Document each wireless scenario separately: employee corporate Wi-Fi, shared-device Wi-Fi, guest access, and any special-purpose SSIDs such as warehouse or kiosk networks.
- Prefer certificate-based authentication such as EAP-TLS for enterprise wireless where possible; if you do, deploy trusted root and client certificate profiles before the Wi-Fi profile.
- Create platform-specific Wi-Fi profiles in the Microsoft Intune admin center and define the SSID, authentication method, proxy settings, and whether the network should connect automatically or only when in range.
- Align Wi-Fi design with network segmentation: devices that fail compliance or device health requirements should not continue to receive the same level of network access as compliant devices.
- Pilot with multiple hardware vendors and roaming scenarios, because adapter drivers, captive portals, certificate stores, and saved profile precedence can all affect user experience.
- Monitor profile deployment and create a rollback plan so you can quickly remove a bad profile without leaving users stranded.

## Reference

Tasks.Name: Intune Tunnel (Strict Tunnel Mode)
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Tunnel-based access for enrolled mobile devices should provide private-resource connectivity without giving every device unrestricted network reach. In a Zero Trust design, the preferred pattern is usually per-app or tightly scoped private access, integrated with Microsoft Intune compliance and Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, so only trusted users on healthy devices can reach the specific services they need.

## Implementation Guidance

1. Define the access target before choosing the tunnel design. Some apps need full network reachability, but many only require access to a small number of internal APIs, web apps, or name spaces.
2. Use the current Microsoft architecture where possible, such as Microsoft Tunnel for mobile application management or another supported Intune VPN profile approach. Avoid broad always-on tunnels unless the business requirement truly needs them.
3. Plan certificate authentication, DNS, split-tunnel behavior, and gateway placement. The most common operational failures are name resolution, certificate lifecycle gaps, and routes that are broader than intended.
4. Assign tunnel access only to enrolled devices that also meet compliance requirements. Pair the design with Conditional Access so a risky or noncompliant device loses access automatically.
5. Pilot with the real apps that depend on the tunnel and measure reconnect behavior, battery impact, captive portal handling, and supportability off the corporate network.
6. Document emergency troubleshooting steps for gateway outage, expired certificates, and app-specific exceptions.

## Reference

Tasks.Name: Remote Help: Android
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

**Remote Help** in Microsoft Intune is a cloud-based remote assistance solution that enables IT support staff to securely view and control managed Windows, macOS, and Android devices using Microsoft Entra ID authentication and granular Intune RBAC controls.

Major 2025–2026 updates include:
- **Included in Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 (June 2026):** Remote Help is now included directly in **Microsoft 365 E3 (EMS E3)** and **Microsoft 365 E5** (as well as Intune Plan 2 / Intune Suite) without requiring a separate standalone add-on purchase.
- **Unattended Remote Help Sessions on Windows (August 2026 / 2608):** Authorized helpdesk agents can now initiate unattended Remote Help sessions on physical Windows devices, signing in with their own credentials to view, control, and troubleshoot devices without requiring an end user to be present.
- **Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) RemoteApp Support (June 2026 / 2606):** Helpdesk agents can securely view and control applications running inside AVD RemoteApp and desktop sessions.
- **US Government GCC High Support (September 2026 / 2609):** Extends Remote Help across Windows, macOS, and Android to GCC High environments.
- **macOS 26 & Microsoft AutoUpdate (MAU) Integration (March 2026):** Remote Help on macOS registers with MAU for automatic client updates and full inventory version reporting.
- **Real-Time Notification Infrastructure:** Uses `*.trouter.communications.svc.cloud.microsoft` (logged in `NotificationInfra.log`) for faster session initiation.

## Implementation Guidance

### Establish the support control model
- Define who can provide remote assistance, whether elevation is allowed, and which device platforms are in scope.
- Use Microsoft Entra groups and Intune role-based access control to separate first-line support from higher-privilege administrators.
- Review Conditional Access requirements for support staff accounts, especially MFA and compliant device requirements.

### Deploy the service
- Enable Remote Help in Intune, assign the required roles, and deploy the Remote Help application or prerequisites to support staff and end-user devices as needed.
- Pilot with helpdesk staff using real support scenarios such as enrollment troubleshooting, policy refresh issues, and app installation failures.
- Confirm user prompts, consent flows, and session logging behavior before announcing the capability broadly.

### Operate securely
- Require support sessions to originate from managed, compliant admin devices rather than personal endpoints.
- Train support teams on when to use Remote Help versus device actions such as sync, collect diagnostics, or wipe.
- Review session usage and any elevation events as part of periodic privileged access governance.

Tasks.Name: Store app deployment
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Store app deployment for Android in Microsoft Intune typically uses Managed Google Play as the governed source for public applications. This allows administrators to approve apps centrally, synchronize them into Intune, and assign them to users or devices with consistent lifecycle management.
In a Zero Trust model, store apps should still be part of a controlled path: approved app source, approved version or update strategy, appropriate app configuration, and access controls that limit corporate data exposure inside the app.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Connect the tenant to Managed Google Play if that prerequisite has not already been completed.
2. Approve only the apps that have passed business and security review, and confirm whether any permissions or in-app dependencies affect the deployment experience.
3. Synchronize approved apps into Intune, then choose the correct assignment intent: required, available, or uninstall.
4. Where supported, pair store app deployment with app configuration policies, managed app settings, and app protection policies so users land in the secure configuration immediately.
5. Use pilot groups and phased rollout for critical apps rather than assigning to the entire population on day one.
6. Monitor install status, version drift, and sign-in failures, and coordinate with app owners when vendor updates change behavior.

## Reference
- **[Connect Intune account to managed Google Play account - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-enrollment/android/connect-managed-google-play)** — Shows how to connect your Intune tenant to Managed Google Play for Android Enterprise management.
- **[Add and Assign Managed Google Play Apps to Android Enterprise Devices - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/deployment/add-managed-google-play)** — Shows how to add, sync, and assign Managed Google Play apps in Microsoft Intune.

Tasks.Name: LoB App Deployment (Direct APK & DDM)
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Line-of-business app deployment in Intune covers internally developed or organization-specific mobile apps that are not simply consumed as public store apps. These apps often carry higher business criticality because they support internal workflows, field operations, or direct access to private business services.
For Zero Trust, LOB apps should be distributed through the most governable path available, combined with secure authentication, app configuration, and strict data-handling controls. For Android, many organizations should evaluate private apps in Managed Google Play before defaulting to raw package deployment.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Decide whether the app should be distributed as a private Managed Google Play app or as a direct Intune line-of-business package. Prefer the more supportable lifecycle when either option is viable.
2. Ensure the package is consistently signed and versioned. Changing signing approach midstream can break update paths and force reinstallation.
3. Document dependencies such as required certificates, private network access, minimum OS level, managed app configuration, and supported device modes.
4. Use phased rollout and a rollback plan for every release, especially if the app is business critical or used by frontline workers.
5. Pair the app with Conditional Access, app protection, or compliant-device requirements when the app handles sensitive corporate data.
6. Track crashes, install failures, and version adoption so app owners and endpoint admins can respond before operations are disrupted.

## Video Walkthrough

Tasks.Name: Web App Deployment
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Web app deployment in Intune usually means publishing a managed shortcut to a business web application or internal portal so users can find and launch it easily from a managed experience. This can be useful for intranet sites, SaaS portals, or lightweight apps that do not justify a full native mobile package.
In Zero Trust terms, publishing the shortcut is only part of the control. You also need to define which browser is supported, how sign-in works, whether the site requires a compliant device, and whether access to private resources depends on an additional control such as Microsoft Tunnel or another secure access method.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Decide whether the target should open in a managed browser such as Microsoft Edge and whether browser policy is needed to protect session data, downloads, and link handling.
2. Create the web app or web link in Intune with a clear name, icon, and audience so users understand what business purpose it serves.
3. Apply Conditional Access appropriate to the site: compliant device, approved client app, MFA, or other grant controls based on the sensitivity of the resource.
4. If the web app is private, verify the access path before rollout. Some sites need Microsoft Tunnel or another private-access pattern rather than a plain internet browser launch.
5. Pilot on the exact mobile platforms and enrollment types you support, validating SSO, redirection, deep links, file handling, and session timeout behavior.
6. Review usage and support tickets after rollout to determine whether the web experience is sufficient or whether a native or private app pattern is needed later.

## Reference

- **[Manage Microsoft Edge on iOS and Android With Intune - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/configuration/configure-edge-ios-android)** — Covers Intune configuration and management options for Microsoft Edge on mobile devices.

Tasks.Name: AppConfig Policies
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
App configuration policies and app protection policies solve different problems in Microsoft Intune. App configuration policies preconfigure how an app behaves, such as account settings, service endpoints, feature flags, or app-specific options. App protection policies control how work data is accessed, moved, encrypted, or wiped inside supported apps. In Zero Trust, the strongest mobile-app design often uses both: configuration to make the managed experience consistent, and protection to keep corporate data contained.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Use app configuration policies when you want to remove manual setup or standardize how supported apps connect and behave for managed users.
2. Use app protection policies when the requirement is to protect organizational data inside the app, such as requiring a PIN, restricting save-as locations, limiting copy and paste, or enabling selective wipe.
3. For personally owned devices, evaluate whether app protection without full device enrollment is sufficient for the workload. This is a common Zero Trust pattern for mobile BYOD access.
4. For corporate-owned devices, combine device management, app configuration, and app protection where the data sensitivity justifies layered controls.
5. Test the user journey from first launch through sign-in, data sharing, and offboarding. The most common failures happen where app configuration and app protection assumptions do not line up.
6. Document app exceptions explicitly. Some business apps support one policy type better than the other, and unsupported assumptions create rollout delays.

Tasks.Name: User enrollment
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
Apple **user enrollment** is designed for personally owned iOS/iPadOS devices where the organization wants a stronger management relationship than app-protection-only access, but without full corporate-style control of the device. It creates a managed work boundary and limits what administrators can see and control, which makes it appropriate for privacy-sensitive BYOD scenarios.

In a Zero Trust design, user enrollment is a middle ground between no device management and full corporate enrollment.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Decide whether user enrollment is actually necessary. If the main requirement is to protect Microsoft 365 data in a small set of apps, **app protection policies** may be simpler.
2. If enrollment is needed, compare the supported Apple user-enrollment methods for your environment, including account-driven options where supported.
3. Document the limitations up front: not every configuration profile, certificate scenario, or remote action available for fully managed devices is available with user enrollment.
4. In the **Microsoft Intune admin center**, create the enrollment profile, scope it to the right users, and test required app delivery plus access controls.
5. Align Conditional Access and compliance expectations with what user-enrolled devices can actually report or enforce.
6. Publish user-facing privacy guidance so employees understand the organization manages the work context, not the full personal device.

## Reference

Tasks.Name: Apple Managed Accounts
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
For personally owned Apple devices, organizations can use **account-driven user enrollment** to provide a lighter-touch management experience that respects personal privacy while still protecting work data. Separately, **Managed Apple IDs** and Apple Business Manager federation can improve how Apple services and identity align with Microsoft Entra ID.

A Zero Trust design should be explicit about which problem is being solved: identity alignment with Apple services, BYOD enrollment with limited management, or both.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Confirm that BYOD users truly need device enrollment rather than only **app protection policies**. If app-level protection is sufficient, MAM-only may provide a better privacy and user-experience balance.
2. If you need Apple BYOD enrollment, evaluate **account-driven user enrollment** and confirm prerequisites such as Apple Business Manager support, supported OS versions, Microsoft Authenticator requirements, and any **just-in-time registration** prerequisites documented by Microsoft.
3. If Managed Apple IDs are part of the design, coordinate with the Apple Business Manager administrators to configure federation and identity lifecycle processes.
4. Create the enrollment profile in the **Microsoft Intune admin center**, target a pilot group, and validate sign-in, app deployment, and removal of work data at unenrollment.
5. Communicate the privacy boundary clearly: user enrollment gives the organization limited management of the work context, not full control of the personal device.
6. Test how the enrollment model interacts with Conditional Access, required apps, certificate delivery, and per-app VPN if those features are in scope.

## Reference

Tasks.Name: ABM Provisioning & Enrollment Time Grouping
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
For corporate-owned Apple devices, **Automated Device Enrollment** through **Apple Business Manager** or **Apple School Manager** is usually the preferred provisioning model. It lets devices enroll into Microsoft Intune during initial setup, supports supervised management, and gives administrators stronger control over required apps, configuration, and security posture from day one.

This is a strong Zero Trust starting point because corporate-owned devices can be brought under management before the user begins normal work.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Connect Apple Business Manager to Intune using the enrollment token and validate synchronization of device records.
2. Import and assign devices in Apple Business Manager so the correct devices are available for Intune enrollment.
3. Create an **Automated Device Enrollment** profile in Intune that defines setup-assistant behavior, whether user affinity is required, supervision, and any shared-device considerations.
4. Decide which required apps, compliance policies, certificates, Wi-Fi, and VPN profiles must be available as early as possible in the provisioning flow.
5. Pilot wipe-and-reprovision scenarios, replacement devices, and reseller-assigned devices. Enrollment strategy is incomplete if only the happy path works.
6. Keep terminology current: use **Automated Device Enrollment** and **Apple Business Manager**, not older DEP branding except where historical mapping is needed.

## Reference

Tasks.Name: Personally Owned Work Profile (AMAPI & Web Enroll)
Dedicated Device (Kiosk Mode)
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

**Microsoft Managed Home Screen (MHS)** is the custom launcher application used on **Android Enterprise corporate-owned dedicated devices (COSU)**, **corporate-owned Dedicated devices with Microsoft Entra Shared Device Mode**, and **fully managed (COBO)** devices to provide a locked-down single-app or multi-app kiosk experience.

Key 2025–2026 security and manageability enhancements to Managed Home Screen include:
- **Require MHS Authentication for Protected App Activities (September 2026 / 2609):** Prevents users from bypassing Managed Home Screen authentication when accessing protected activities inside MAM-integrated apps. If MHS requires sign-in or a session PIN, the app automatically redirects the user back to MHS to authenticate before allowing access to organizational content.
- **Silence Apps During MHS Lock / Session PIN Prompt (June 2026 / 2605):** Admins can configure MHS to silence background apps whenever MHS prompts for authentication (at sign-in or the session PIN screen). Silenced apps cannot start activities, show notifications, appear in recent apps, or pop dialogs/toasts to bypass the lock screen. Admins can define an allowlist for critical communication apps (such as voice/calling apps).
- **Remote Actions to Temporarily Suspend and Restore MHS (April 2026 / 2604):** Helpdesk admins can trigger **Suspend Managed Home Screen** from the Intune admin center to let a technician or user exit kiosk mode to the native launcher for a defined time window without revealing the exit PIN or removing policies. MHS automatically re-locks when the timer expires or when **Restore Managed Home Screen** is triggered.
- **Device Configuration Profile Required for Exit Lock Task Mode Password (June 2026 / 2605):** The MHS exit lock task mode password must now be configured via an Android Enterprise **Device Configuration profile** rather than an app configuration policy.
- **Custom Top Bar Elements & Expanded Volume Sliders (2511 / 2605):** Supports custom free-text strings with dynamic variables (`{{SerialNumber}}`, `{{DeviceName}}`, `{{TenantName}}`) in the top bar and granular sliders for call, ring/notification, and alarm volumes.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Use Managed Home Screen primarily with Android Enterprise dedicated devices and other supported shared or task-oriented scenarios.
2. Deploy the Managed Home Screen app from Managed Google Play and assign it together with the apps that workers actually need for their role.
3. Create app configuration policies for Managed Home Screen to define layout, sign-in expectations, PIN or session settings, virtual home screen behavior, and any approved links or widgets.
4. Combine Managed Home Screen with kiosk and device restriction settings so users cannot leave the intended workflow or access unsupported settings.
5. Pilot with actual frontline users to validate navigation, barcode or camera flows, sign-in friction, app launch performance, and recovery after a restart.
6. Document support steps for cache reset, launcher updates, and device reprovisioning so help desk can restore service quickly.

## Reference

Tasks.Name: AOSP (Android Open Source Project)
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Android Open Source Project (AOSP) device management in Microsoft Intune is aimed at specialized Android devices that do not use Google Mobile Services. These devices are common in logistics, manufacturing, healthcare, and other dedicated-use scenarios. From a Zero Trust perspective, AOSP management matters because organizations still need identity, app control, update discipline, and compliance signals even when the device ecosystem does not look like a standard Android Enterprise deployment with Managed Google Play.

## Implementation Guidance

1. Use AOSP only when the hardware or operational model requires it. If a supported device can run a standard Android Enterprise fully managed or corporate-owned dedicated deployment, that option is often easier to support and secure.
2. Confirm the exact AOSP enrollment mode supported by Microsoft Intune for the device type. Document the enrollment token process, expected user association model, and who is responsible for re-enrollment if a device is wiped or replaced.
3. Plan app delivery early. Because AOSP devices do not use Google Play in the usual way, you may rely on line-of-business packages, vendor distribution methods, or tightly controlled browser access.
4. Validate how the device handles certificates, Wi-Fi, VPN, kiosk mode, peripherals, and OEM-specific controls. For rugged endpoints, barcode scanners, printers, camera workflows, and hardware buttons often matter more than standard mobile UX.
5. Apply the narrowest identity and resource access model possible. Many AOSP devices are shared or task specific, so user entitlements and device entitlements should be intentionally constrained.
6. Test update and replacement operations in the field. AOSP devices are often remote, shift based, and business critical, so supportability is as important as enrollment success.

## Reference

- **[Android device enrollment guide for Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-enrollment/android/guide)** — Includes AOSP enrollment guidance for Android devices managed by Intune.
- **[Add Apps to Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/deployment/)** — Explains how to add app types in Intune, including line-of-business apps.

Tasks.Name: Shared iPad
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
**Shared iPad** is an Apple capability for supported supervised iPads that allows multiple users to sign in to the same device while keeping their apps and data separated in local partitions. In Microsoft Intune, Shared iPad is appropriate for education, clinical, retail, and other shift-based or communal-use cases where users need a more personalized experience than a simple kiosk provides.

From a Zero Trust perspective, Shared iPad helps preserve user separation on a physically shared device, but it still requires careful planning for identity, app support, compliance, and sign-out behavior.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Confirm that the use case truly requires **Shared iPad** rather than standard assigned iPads or **Microsoft Entra shared device mode** for supported apps.
2. Use a supervised Apple enrollment path, typically through **Apple Business Manager** or **Apple School Manager**, and create the appropriate Intune enrollment profile for Shared iPad.
3. If you plan to use **Managed Apple IDs** and federation with Microsoft Entra ID, coordinate identity setup with the Apple administrators before rollout.
4. Pilot sign-in speed, local storage capacity, app behavior across multiple users, and what happens when the device is offline or full.
5. Validate Conditional Access, required apps, certificates, and any classroom or frontline workflows with real devices before scaling.
6. Train support staff on how Shared iPad differs from Shared Device Mode and on when wiping or reassigning a device is necessary.

## Reference
- **[Shared iPad devices in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/mem/intune/enrollment/device-enrollment-shared-ipad)**
- **[Shared iOS and iPadOS devices in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/mem/intune/enrollment/device-enrollment-shared-ios)**

Tasks.Name: Entra Shared Device Mode
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview
**Microsoft Entra shared device mode** is designed for supported mobile applications on devices that are handed from one worker to another, especially in frontline scenarios. It enables a coordinated sign-in and sign-out experience across participating apps so local work data can be reduced when shifts change.

This is valuable in Zero Trust because trust should follow the active user session, not linger from the previous user on a shared device.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Confirm that the business scenario is truly a **shared-user** scenario rather than a dedicated kiosk or a standard assigned corporate device.
2. Verify that the apps users need actually support **shared device mode**. The feature depends on participating apps and identity integration, not only on Intune policy.
3. Choose the enrollment path that supports your device type and management goals, such as an appropriate corporate-owned mobile enrollment model for the platform.
4. Design the sign-in/out workflow carefully: inactivity timeout, handoff between shifts, what happens offline, and how leftover session data is removed.
5. Deploy required apps, configuration, and Conditional Access policies that match the shared-device scenario.
6. Document clearly that **shared device mode** is different from **Shared iPad**. Shared device mode focuses on app session behavior; Shared iPad creates multiple user partitions on supported iPads.

## Reference
- **[Shared device mode overview - Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/msal-shared-devices)**
- **[Set up automated device enrollment for shared device mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/mem/intune/enrollment/automated-device-enrollment-shared-device-mode)**
- **[Shared device mode for Android devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/msal/android/shared-devices)** — Covers Microsoft Entra shared device mode for frontline worker scenarios.

Tasks.Name: Compliance: Require Firewall
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Managing the macOS firewall through Intune helps enforce baseline host protection on managed Macs. It is one of the controls that prevents the endpoint from depending entirely on network perimeter assumptions, which is important for remote and mobile users.

In Zero Trust, the intent is to keep device exposure low, especially on untrusted networks, while still allowing approved apps and management traffic to function predictably.

## Implementation Guidance

### Define the desired firewall state
- Decide whether the built-in macOS application firewall should be enabled for all managed Macs and whether stealth mode or similar hardening settings are required.
- Document any approved exceptions and the business reason for them before deployment.
- Review how firewall policy interacts with developer tools, peer-to-peer workflows, or remote support utilities used in the organization.

### Configure through Intune
- Use the supported macOS endpoint security Firewall policy or settings catalog settings in the Microsoft Intune admin center, depending on which settings are needed.
- Separate baseline firewall enablement from higher-risk exceptions so changes can be governed independently.
- Pilot the policy on devices with representative app stacks and network conditions before broad rollout.

### Monitor and refine
- Track user impact and support cases to identify legitimate app communication issues caused by the new policy.
- Review profile deployment results and device-side logs when troubleshooting inconsistent behavior.
- Revisit exceptions periodically to ensure temporary allowances are removed.

## Reference

- **[Manage firewall settings with endpoint security policies in Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-configuration/endpoint-security/firewall)** — Explains Intune endpoint security firewall policies, including settings relevant to macOS.

Tasks.Name: Defender for macOS
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

For macOS, antivirus and endpoint detection and response are typically delivered through Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, with Intune used to deploy the app and the supporting configuration required by macOS. This gives security teams visibility and protection across Apple endpoints that participate in Microsoft security operations.

In Zero Trust, AV and EDR provide device-health and threat posture signals that complement enrollment and compliance. A managed Mac should not only be enrolled; it should also be capable of detecting, preventing, and reporting malicious behavior.

## Implementation Guidance

### Prepare the macOS security prerequisites
- Confirm that devices meet the supported macOS version and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint requirements before assignment.
- Plan the necessary configuration profiles for system extensions, network extensions, notifications, background services, and full disk access where required.
- Coordinate with the Microsoft Defender security team so onboarding packages, tenant association, and alert routing are ready before rollout.

### Deploy the service through Intune
- Package or assign the Defender for Endpoint app in Intune using the supported macOS app type and deployment method.
- Create the prerequisite macOS configuration profiles first so users are not prompted manually for permissions that should be managed by policy.
- Assign the EDR or onboarding policy only after the client and prerequisites are confirmed on pilot devices.

### Validate protection outcomes
- Confirm the device appears in both Intune and Microsoft Defender with the expected health state and sensor onboarding status.
- Test malware detection and policy enforcement in a safe validation method approved by the security team.
- Review update cadence, exclusion governance, and device performance feedback before broad deployment.

## Reference

- **[Configure Microsoft Defender for Endpoint with Intune and onboard devices - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/configure-integration)** — Explains how to connect Intune and onboard macOS devices to Defender for Endpoint.
- **[Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on macOS - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/microsoft-defender-endpoint-mac)** — Describes Defender for Endpoint capabilities and deployment considerations for macOS.

Tasks.Name: Apple Business Manager
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

For corporate-owned Macs, Apple Business Manager (ABM) with Automated Device Enrollment (ADE) is the preferred provisioning model for Microsoft Intune. It provides a controlled out-of-box experience, ensures the device enters management during setup, and reduces the chance that security controls are bypassed before the user reaches production resources.

Within Zero Trust, ADE supports a stronger trust chain because the device identity, enrollment ownership, and first-run configuration are established in a predictable and supportable way.

## Implementation Guidance

### Prepare the Apple and Microsoft prerequisites
- Maintain a valid Apple MDM push certificate and connect Intune to Apple Business Manager using an enrollment token for Automated Device Enrollment.
- Ensure corporate-purchased Macs are assigned in ABM to the correct MDM server and reviewed before shipment to users.
- Decide which Setup Assistant screens should be shown or skipped and whether modern authentication or Company Portal sign-in is required for the user journey.

### Create and assign the enrollment design
- Create macOS ADE enrollment profiles in the Microsoft Intune admin center and scope them to the correct device groups or token assignments.
- Align ADE with downstream requirements such as FileVault, Platform SSO, Defender for Endpoint, and software update policy so the device reaches a secure state quickly after first sign-in.
- Pilot with new devices and with wiped-and-reprovisioned devices to validate the full lifecycle experience.

### Operate the provisioning process
- Monitor token expiration, ADE profile assignment success, and first-run enrollment failures as part of standard service operations.
- Use documented warehouse or reseller workflows so devices are not shipped before ABM assignment is complete.
- Establish a fallback plan for exceptions such as repair replacements or preexisting Macs that were not purchased through standard channels.

## Reference

- **[Step 5 – Enroll devices in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-enrollment/enroll-devices)** — Covers Apple automated device enrollment for corporate-owned Mac devices in Intune.

Tasks.Name: Local Account Management
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Local account management on macOS should support the device lifecycle without undermining identity-based control. Most organizations need a consistent approach for the primary user account, support or break-glass accounts, and whether any standing local administrator rights remain on standard user devices.

In Zero Trust, the local account model matters because unmanaged administrator access or poorly governed secondary accounts can bypass the broader security design even when the device is enrolled and compliant.

## Implementation Guidance

### Define the local account model
- Decide whether standard users should receive local admin rights; the preferred pattern is usually no standing local admin for everyday users.
- Document which local accounts are required for support, recovery, or provisioning and how their passwords are controlled.
- Align the account strategy with Platform SSO, FileVault, and enrollment so the first-run experience remains supportable.

### Configure through Intune
- Use supported macOS account configuration settings in Intune to create or manage local accounts only where there is a clear business requirement.
- Avoid embedding reusable shared credentials in policy content unless the design explicitly addresses secret rotation and exposure risk.
- Pilot account creation, privilege level, and first sign-in behavior on test devices before production rollout.

### Review and reduce privilege over time
- Audit which users retain local admin rights and move recurring elevation needs to a more controlled model where possible.
- Coordinate password rotation and recovery processes with the service desk before using secondary admin accounts widely.
- Treat local account exceptions as temporary and review them regularly.

## Reference

- **[Deployment guide to manage macOS devices in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/fundamentals/platform-guide-macos)** — Provides a macOS-focused Intune deployment guide covering enrollment, policies, and app deployment.

Tasks.Name: Platform SSO (ADE Setup Registration)
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

For modern macOS identity experiences, organizations should evaluate Microsoft Entra Platform SSO rather than treating the feature as just a generic 'SSO extension.' Platform SSO can improve sign-in consistency, strengthen device-to-identity integration, and reduce repeated prompts for managed Macs.

In a Zero Trust design, the value of Platform SSO is not convenience alone. It can improve confidence that the signed-in user, device registration state, and downstream access controls are aligned before access is granted to business resources.

## Implementation Guidance

### Confirm prerequisites and target scenario
- Verify the supported macOS version, Intune Company Portal version, Microsoft Entra configuration prerequisites, and hardware capabilities for the chosen Platform SSO mode.
- Decide whether the goal is password synchronization, passwordless sign-in, secure enclave-backed credentials, or another supported pattern.
- Limit the initial pilot to corporate-owned, fully managed devices unless there is a strong reason to test broader scenarios first.

### Deploy Platform SSO in Intune
- Create the appropriate macOS configuration profile in the Microsoft Intune admin center and configure the Platform SSO settings according to the supported Microsoft Entra scenario.
- Coordinate with enrollment, local account creation, FileVault, and compliance policy so the user journey remains coherent from first sign-in onward.
- Test first-run registration, sign-in prompts, password changes, and app access for Microsoft 365 and other federated applications.

### Operate and support
- Prepare support staff to troubleshoot registration failures, stale credentials, and device re-registration scenarios.
- Monitor adoption and sign-in behavior before expanding the rollout to all managed Macs.
- Review whether Platform SSO changes local account expectations or break-glass admin processes.

Tasks.Name: EPM for macOS
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

**Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM)** allows organizations to enforce least privilege by running all users as standard users (without local administrator rights) while providing policy-controlled, just-in-time elevation for specific applications and tasks.

Key 2025–2026 updates to EPM include:
- **Included in Microsoft 365 E5 (June 2026 / 2606):** EPM is now included in **Microsoft 365 E5** (in addition to the Microsoft Intune Suite), enabling broad enterprise adoption without a separate add-on license.
- **Elevate as Current User (October 2025 / 2510):** Elevation rules now support an **Elevate as current user** option (in addition to virtual account elevation). This runs the elevated process under the signed-in user's own account after requiring Windows Authentication (supporting MFA), preserving the user's profile paths, environment variables, and audit trail consistency.
- **Expanded Support-Approved Elevations on Shared Devices (April 2026 / 2604):** Support-approved file elevation requests are now supported from **all users of a device**, not just the primary or enrolling user—unlocking EPM for shared workstations.
- **Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) Support (February 2026 / 2601):** EPM elevation policies now support deployment to users on AVD single-session virtual machines.
- **EPM Readiness & Elevation Trends Dashboard (2510):** Surfaces insights on managed vs. unmanaged elevations to identify which users are ready to transition from local admin to standard user.
- **Scope Tag Enforcement & System Proxy Support (2511 / 2604):** Enforces RBAC scope tags on EPM elevation requests and EPM reports, and supports telemetry reporting over system-level (`WinHTTP`) proxies.

## Implementation Guidance

### Define the least-privilege target state
- Identify which users still have local admin rights, which tasks truly require elevation, and which apps should be remediated instead of permanently excepted.
- Decide whether elevations should be automatic for trusted rules, user-approved with justification, or handled by support staff through a separate process.
- Review licensing and device support requirements before planning deployment beyond a pilot population.

### Configure EPM in Intune
- Deploy the EPM client settings and create elevation rules that are as specific as possible, using publisher, file hash, path, or other supported attributes.
- Prefer narrowly scoped rules for approved installers, management tools, or update workflows instead of broad path-based allow rules.
- Pilot with users who frequently need admin actions so support can validate prompt behavior, success rates, and audit detail.

### Operate and review elevation activity
- Review elevation reports and justifications regularly to identify apps that should be packaged differently or workflows that can be redesigned.
- Expire temporary exceptions and remove unused rules so the EPM rule set does not grow into a shadow admin model.
- Coordinate EPM with Windows LAPS, local admin removal, and helpdesk procedures so the operating model stays consistent.

## Reference

- [Support-approved file elevations for Endpoint Privilege Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/epm/manage-support-approvals)
