Tasks.Name: FileVault
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

FileVault provides full-disk encryption for macOS and is a foundational control for protecting data at rest on corporate-managed Macs. In a Zero Trust device program, FileVault reduces the impact of device loss or theft and helps ensure that local data is not easily exposed outside approved access paths.

A good FileVault deployment plan covers enablement timing, recovery key escrow, user communication, and support procedures. Encryption should be part of the standard enrollment and provisioning model for corporate-owned Macs unless a documented exception exists.

## Implementation Guidance

### Define the encryption standard
- Decide which Macs must use FileVault, whether enablement should be immediate or deferred for a limited number of sign-ins, and how recovery keys will be escrowed and accessed.
- Establish who may retrieve recovery keys and how those retrievals will be audited.
- Review interactions with local account creation, Platform SSO, and break-glass admin accounts before rollout.

### Configure FileVault in Intune
- Create the supported macOS FileVault or endpoint security disk encryption profile in the Microsoft Intune admin center.
- Configure recovery key settings and assign the profile to pilot devices first to validate the end-user experience and escrow flow.
- Confirm that recovery keys are visible where expected and that support staff know how to handle recovery events securely.

### Operate and support
- Monitor encryption status and investigate devices that do not complete enablement or escrow their recovery key.
- Document recovery procedures for password reset, hardware repair, and employee departure scenarios.
- Review exceptions such as lab devices or shared devices separately so they do not weaken the baseline standard.

## Video Walkthrough

Tasks.Name: Company Portal Deployment
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

App management for macOS in Intune should focus on packaging, assignment, dependency handling, update planning, and access to required business applications on managed Macs. Common app types include macOS package apps, Microsoft apps, line-of-business apps, web links, and Company Portal-delivered experiences.

In a Zero Trust endpoint strategy, app management supports the principle that only approved software should be delivered to trusted devices and that access to business apps should be paired with device identity, compliance, and least-privilege controls.

## Implementation Guidance

### Plan the app portfolio
- Inventory required macOS apps and classify them as core productivity apps, security agents, browser components, developer tools, or department-specific software.
- Decide which apps are required, available for self-service, or intentionally blocked from unmanaged distribution paths.
- Confirm packaging and update ownership for each app so critical software does not rely on manual user installs.

### Deploy through Intune
- Use the supported macOS app type in Intune for each package, and test installation, uninstall, and upgrade behavior on pilot devices before broad targeting.
- Sequence security agents, identity components, and user-facing apps in a way that supports the desired day-one device experience.
- Use device or user group assignment intentionally and document why an app is required versus optional.

### Operate the app lifecycle
- Monitor install status, failed deployments, and version drift so high-value applications remain current.
- Do not assume mobile-style Intune app protection policies apply to native macOS apps; instead, rely on device management, app configuration where supported, and identity or access controls.
- Review whether unsupported or side-loaded apps need separate control through application allow or block strategies.

## Reference

- **[Add an Unmanaged macOS PKG App to Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/deployment/add-unmanaged-pkg-macos)** — Covers uploading and deploying macOS PKG line-of-business apps in Microsoft Intune.
- **[Deployment guide to manage macOS devices in Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/fundamentals/platform-guide-macos)** — Provides guidance on deploying apps, profiles, and compliance policies for macOS devices in Intune.
- **[Use Shell Scripts on macOS Devices in Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/tools/run-shell-scripts-macos)** — Shows how to deploy and manage shell scripts on Intune-managed Macs.

Tasks.Name: Resource Access (Certificates, VPN, Network Configs)
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Certificates, Wi-Fi, and VPN profiles are foundational connectivity controls for managed macOS devices. When designed together, they can deliver certificate-based trust to corporate networks and reduce dependence on reusable passwords for device connectivity.

In a Zero Trust model, the goal is not simply automatic connectivity. The goal is to ensure that only managed, appropriately trusted devices can establish network access paths and that those paths align with compliance and identity controls.

## Implementation Guidance

### Design the certificate trust model
- Decide whether certificates will be issued from Microsoft Cloud PKI, an existing enterprise PKI, or another trusted source, and confirm which use cases each authority will support.
- Choose the authentication methods required for Wi-Fi and VPN, such as certificate-based authentication, and align them with network team requirements.
- Document certificate lifetimes, renewal behavior, revocation expectations, and dependencies on device identity or user identity.

### Build dependent profiles in Intune
- Create and test certificate profiles first, because Wi-Fi and VPN profiles often depend on the certificate being present and trusted.
- Create separate Wi-Fi and VPN profiles in Intune for distinct use cases, such as campus wireless, privileged admin access, or always-on remote connectivity.
- Pilot connectivity on representative networks before wide rollout so profile logic, trust chains, and DNS behavior can be validated.

### Operate and troubleshoot
- Monitor certificate issuance, profile deployment, and failed connection reports together instead of treating each as an isolated problem space.
- Coordinate certificate rollover and root trust changes carefully to avoid widespread connectivity loss.
- Review whether some access paths should move to modern app-layer access controls rather than remaining on broad network VPN access.

## Reference

- **[Use SCEP certificate profiles with Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-configuration/certificates/scep-profiles)** — Explains how to create and assign SCEP certificate profiles in Intune.

Tasks.Name: Device Restrictions
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

The Intune settings catalog provides a broad, searchable way to configure macOS device settings without relying exclusively on older profile templates. It is useful when you need more granular configuration and want to standardize policy creation in a single management plane.

For Zero Trust, settings catalog profiles help enforce consistent security controls on managed Macs, but they must be designed carefully so multiple teams do not create overlapping profiles that conflict or become hard to troubleshoot.

## Implementation Guidance

### Design the profile structure
- Group settings by purpose, such as security baseline, privacy permissions, authentication experience, or user experience, instead of creating one oversized profile.
- Establish a naming standard and ownership model so admins can identify which team manages each profile.
- Review whether a setting already exists in another template or baseline before adding it to a new settings catalog profile.

### Configure and assign
- Create the macOS settings catalog profile in the Microsoft Intune admin center and add only the settings that are needed for the target outcome.
- Use test groups first and validate the device-side behavior, especially for privacy preferences, login items, background services, and restrictions that may affect end-user workflows.
- Document settings that intentionally differ by department or device role so those differences are not mistaken for policy drift.

### Monitor and maintain
- Use profile reporting and support diagnostics to identify unsupported settings, conflicts, and assignment issues.
- Retire template-based or custom-profile duplicates when an equivalent settings catalog implementation replaces them.
- Review macOS release notes regularly because available settings and behaviors can change with new operating system versions.

## Reference

- **[Create a policy using settings catalog in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-configuration/settings-catalog/)** — Explains how to use the Intune settings catalog to create granular device configuration policies.
- **[Deployment guide to manage macOS devices in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/fundamentals/platform-guide-macos)** — Provides a macOS-focused Intune deployment guide that includes device profile creation and policy planning.
- **[Monitor and troubleshoot - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/monitor-troubleshoot)** — Central hub for monitoring device profiles, policy assignment status, and troubleshooting in Microsoft Intune.

Tasks.Name: Managed macOS Updates (DDM)
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Managing software updates on macOS (and iOS/iPadOS) in Microsoft Intune has transitioned to **Apple Declarative Device Management (DDM)**.

> **Important Deprecation Notice (2025–2026):** With the release of iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS 26, Apple deprecated legacy MDM software update commands and payloads. Microsoft Intune is retiring and removing legacy Apple MDM software update workloads (`Devices > Update policies for macOS/iOS` and legacy Software Update settings in Device Restrictions). All Apple software updates must be configured using **DDM in the Intune Settings Catalog**.

### Benefits of DDM Software Updates
1. **Device Autonomy:** The device proactively evaluates and enforces update deadlines locally without relying on continuous MDM server polling.
2. **Assignment Filters Support (March 2026 / 2602):** DDM software update policies in Intune now support **Assignment Filters** (including the GA `operatingSystemVersion` property) to stage updates across rings.
3. **Background Security Improvements:** Supports Apple's rebranded *Background Security Improvements* (formerly *Rapid Security Responses*) and Apple OS 27 DDM status reporting in Device Inventory.

### Key Configuration Steps
1. Sign in to the Microsoft Intune admin center.
2. Go to **Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy**.
3. Select **macOS** (or **iOS/iPadOS**) for platform and **Settings catalog** for profile type.
4. Expand **Declarative Device Management (DDM) > Software Update** and configure the target OS version, target build, and local enforcement date/time.
5. Assign the policy using **Assignment Filters** and retire any legacy MDM Update Policies.

## Reference

- [Manage Apple software updates with Declarative Device Management (DDM) in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-updates/apple/)

Tasks.Name: Scripts
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Scripts in Intune are a gap-closure tool for configuration and remediation tasks that are not yet available through native policy settings. On Windows, PowerShell scripts and related remediation workflows can help enforce standards, collect information, or fix drift when used carefully.

From a Zero Trust perspective, scripts should be used sparingly and governed tightly. A script can strengthen device trust, but it is also executable code running at scale on endpoints, which makes review, scoping, signing, and rollback planning important.

## Implementation Guidance

### Prefer native controls when possible
- Use settings catalog, endpoint security, compliance, and application management features first; use scripts only when Intune does not natively expose the required outcome.
- Define the exact purpose of each script, its expected output, the execution context, and its owner.
- Avoid using scripts as a permanent substitute for a well-supported product feature if a native control becomes available later.

### Develop and deploy safely
- Test scripts on isolated pilot devices and validate 32-bit versus 64-bit execution behavior, rerun behavior, and logging before broad assignment.
- Use the Intune management extension where required and confirm it is healthy on target devices.
- Separate detection logic from remediation logic when using remediation-style workflows so support teams can understand why a device was changed.

### Operate with change control
- Version-control every script, require peer review, and maintain a rollback plan for failures.
- Review execution status, device logs, and helpdesk tickets after deployment to catch unintended side effects quickly.
- Remove or replace scripts that become obsolete so the environment does not accumulate hidden configuration dependencies.

## Reference

- **[Add PowerShell Scripts to Windows Devices in Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/tools/run-powershell-scripts-windows)** — Explains how to upload and run PowerShell scripts on Windows devices by using Intune.
- **[Use Remediations to Detect and Fix Support Issues - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/tools/deploy-remediations)** — Explains how to use Remediations in Intune for detection and corrective scripting workflows.

Tasks.Name: Stage Rollouts with Deployment Plans
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

**Deployment Plans** (introduced in September 2026 under the **Deployments** experience in the Microsoft Intune admin center) enable administrators to roll out applications and configuration policies in controlled stages across multiple rings instead of deploying changes to all targeted devices at once.

Supported workloads include:
- **Windows Applications:** Win32 apps and Enterprise App Catalog (EAM) applications.
- **Windows Policies:** Settings Catalog policies and Endpoint Security policies.

Deployment Plans integrate natively with **Multi-Admin Approval (MAA)**, ensuring that high-impact staged rollouts require secondary administrator authorization before advancing across production device fleets.

This supports *Assume breach* and operational resilience by preventing a misconfigured policy or faulty application update from simultaneously impacting the entire enterprise endpoint estate.

## Key Configuration Steps

1. Navigate to the **Deployments** node in the Microsoft Intune admin center.
2. Define ring groups (e.g., *Ring 0 – Canary/IT*, *Ring 1 – Pilot*, *Ring 2 – Broad Production*) and rollout timing intervals between stages.
3. Enable **Multi-Admin Approval** integration on deployment plans for critical security policies and enterprise-wide applications.
4. Monitor rollout health at each stage and pause or halt progression if anomalies or failures are detected.

## Reference

- [Deployment plans and deployments in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/deployments/overview)

Tasks.Name: Security Copilot Agents in Intune (Agentic ID)
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

**Security Copilot Agents in Intune** are specialized AI agents embedded in the Intune admin center (`Agents` node) that automate complex endpoint security, change review, policy creation, and lifecycle hygiene workflows:

1. **Vulnerability Remediation Agent:** Analyzes Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management exposure data, prioritizes CVE risks, and recommends or deploys Intune remediation actions (app updates or configuration changes).
2. **Change Review Agent:** Evaluates **Multi-Admin Approval (MAA)** requests for Windows PowerShell scripts, surfacing inline risk assessments and contextual explanations of script behavior directly in the MAA approval queue.
3. **Policy Configuration Agent:** Analyzes uploaded compliance documents, regulatory standards, or security benchmarks and maps them directly to recommended Intune Settings Catalog policies.
4. **Device Offboarding Agent:** Identifies stale, inactive, or misaligned device records across Intune and Microsoft Entra ID and guides admins through safe, approval-gated offboarding.

### Microsoft Entra Agentic Identity (2026 Update)
Starting in 2026, Intune Security Copilot agents (such as the Vulnerability Remediation Agent and Policy Configuration Agent) run under dedicated **Microsoft Entra agentic identities** rather than human user accounts. Setup automatically provisions an agentic user identity in Entra ID, allowing admins to scope least-privilege Entra and Defender XDR permissions specifically to the agent and verify setup with the **Run Readiness Check** button.

## Key Configuration Steps

1. Enable Microsoft Intune as a data source in Microsoft Security Copilot (Intune Administrator automatically inherits Security Copilot Owner; other Intune RBAC roles inherit Contributor).
2. Navigate to **Agents** in the Intune admin center and configure the desired agents.
3. Provision or transition each agent to a **Microsoft Entra agentic identity** (mandatory as human user identity support is retired).
4. Assign least-privilege Microsoft Entra and Microsoft Defender XDR Unified RBAC permissions to the agentic identity and run the **Readiness Check**.

## Reference

Tasks.Name: Detect & Block Shadow AI / Local AI Agents
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Unsanctioned local AI agents (such as **OpenClaw**) running directly on endpoints can read local files, execute shell commands, invoke browser sessions, and exfiltrate sensitive organizational data outside cloud governance perimeters. Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint provide a multi-layered Zero Trust defense for local AI agents on Windows devices:

1. **Discover via Properties Catalog & Multi-Device Query (2605):** Collect the **Local AI Agent** entity using an Intune Properties Catalog policy and query fleet-wide presence using KQL **Device Query**.
2. **Prevent Execution via Security Baseline (2605):** Deploy the **Local AI Agent Baseline – OpenClaw (Preview)** (or toggle blocking from the M365 Admin Center Shadow AI page, which auto-creates the `A365 - Block OpenClaw` Intune policy) to block execution paths on managed Windows endpoints.
3. **Runtime Protection via Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (2609):** Configure **MDE AI agent runtime protection** settings in the Windows Endpoint Security template in **Audit** mode (detect and alert on unsafe AI agent activity) or **Block** mode (stop unsafe AI agent actions before execution).
4. **Enforce Access via Compliance Policy & Conditional Access (In Development):** Configure prohibited local AI agents in a Windows **Compliance Policy** so devices with unsanctioned agents are automatically marked noncompliant and blocked from corporate resources by Microsoft Entra Conditional Access until the agent is removed.

## Key Configuration Steps

1. Create an Intune **Properties Catalog** policy (`Devices > Configuration`) to collect the **Local AI Agent** inventory entity and audit devices via **Device Query**.
2. Deploy the **Local AI Agent Baseline - OpenClaw** (or enable blocking in the M365 Admin Center Shadow AI page) to block unsanctioned agent execution.
3. Configure **MDE AI agent runtime protection** (`Endpoint security > Antivirus / Defender for Endpoint`) in Audit or Block mode.
4. Add prohibited AI agent rules to your Windows **Compliance Policy** to enforce Conditional Access blocks on noncompliant endpoints.

## Reference

- [Local AI Agent Baseline - OpenClaw (Preview) settings reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/security-baselines/ref-openclaw-settings)

Tasks.Name: Controlled Configuration for Defender Antivirus
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

**Controlled Configuration for Microsoft Defender Antivirus** (introduced in July 2026 / Service Release 2607) extends Microsoft Defender Tamper Protection by making the Defender Antivirus settings delivered by Microsoft Intune (or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint security settings management) **authoritative** on Windows endpoints.

When Controlled Configuration is enabled, Intune/MDE antivirus policies override and lock out conflicting configurations coming from other channels—such as local Group Policy Objects (GPOs), Configuration Manager, registry edits, or local scripts. This guarantees a consistent, predictable, and tamper-resistant antivirus posture across all managed Windows devices.

This supports *Assume breach* by preventing an attacker with local administrative privileges or legacy GPO access from weakening Defender Antivirus exclusions, real-time protection, or cloud-delivered protection settings.

## Key Configuration Steps

1. Ensure **Tamper Protection** is enabled on Windows endpoints via Microsoft Defender XDR / Intune Endpoint Security.
2. In the Microsoft Intune admin center, go to **Endpoint security > Antivirus** and create or edit a **Microsoft Defender Antivirus** policy for Windows.
3. Enable **Controlled Configuration** in Audit or Enforcement mode after validating that no required legacy GPO or ConfigMgr AV overrides are needed.
4. Monitor policy compliance and Defender status across your Windows device fleet.

## Reference

- [Controlled configuration for Microsoft Defender settings in Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-configuration/endpoint-security/antivirus#controlled-configuration-for-microsoft-defender-settings-preview)

Tasks.Name: Windows Backup & Restore for Organizations
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

**Windows Backup for Organizations** (Generally Available in Intune in November 2025 / February 2026) enables organizations to back up user Windows settings and Microsoft Store app lists to the cloud and seamlessly restore them onto a new or re-provisioned Microsoft Entra joined Windows 11 device.

The restore flow can be initiated:
- **During the Out-of-Box Experience (OOBE)** at the time of Windows Autopilot / Entra join enrollment, or
- **At first sign-in** when a user signs in with their Microsoft Entra ID account after the device finishes enrolling.

Because Windows Backup for Organizations restores user preferences and Store app pointers rather than a full disk image, it accelerates Zero Trust cloud-native device refreshes (moving off legacy domain-joined PCs or recovering from device replacements) without carrying over legacy OS drift or malware persistence.

## Key Configuration Steps

1. In the Microsoft Intune admin center, create a **Windows Settings Catalog** policy (`Devices > Configuration`) and configure **Windows Backup and Restore > Enable Windows Backup** and **Enable Windows Restore**.
2. Navigate to **Devices > Enrollment > Windows > Windows Backup and Restore** to configure the tenant-wide OOBE restore experience.
3. Assign the policy to target Microsoft Entra joined device or user groups.

## Reference

- [Windows Backup for Organizations in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-enrollment/windows/enable-backup-restore)
- [Windows Backup for Organizations overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/configuration/windows-backup)

Tasks.Name: Apple Intelligence & Android AI Data Controls
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Modern mobile and desktop operating systems include deeply integrated on-device and cloud-connected AI assistants (such as **Apple Intelligence** on iOS/iPadOS/macOS and **Google Gemini / Circle to Search / App Functions** on Android). Without explicit MDM and MAM controls, organizational data inside managed apps can be captured via screen context, summarized by external AI workspaces, or manipulated by on-device AI agents.

Key 2025–2026 Intune controls for governing mobile and endpoint AI include:
- **iOS/iPadOS App Protection Policy (MAM) Standalone AI Controls:** Standalone MAM Data Protection settings to selectively block or allow **Genmoji**, **Writing Tools**, and **Screen Capture** (including screen recording and mirroring, with user alert popups on iOS SDK 20.3.0+).
- **Apple Declarative Device Management (DDM) Intelligence Settings (2603 / 2605):** In the Intune Settings Catalog for iOS/iPadOS and macOS (replacing deprecated legacy MDM restrictions in OS 26.4+), admins can granularly govern:
  - **External Intelligence Settings:** *Allow Sign In* and *Allowed Workspace IDs*
  - **Intelligence Settings:** *Allow Writing Tools*, *Allow Genmoji*, *Allow Image Playground / Image Wand*, *Allow Visual Intelligence Summary*, *Mail Smart Replies & Summary*, *Notes Transcription & Summary*, *Safari Summary*, and *Force On-Device Only Dictation/Translation*.
- **Android Enterprise AI & Agent Controls (2510 / 2606):**
  - **Block assist content sharing with privileged apps:** Blocks screenshots and app context from being sent to assistant apps (blocking **Circle to Search**).
  - **Block apps from exposing app functions (2606):** Prevents managed apps on COBO, COSU, and COPE work profiles from exposing programmatic actions (*app functions*) that on-device assistants or AI agents can invoke inside the app.

## Reference

Tasks.Name: Samsung Knox E-FOTA & Corporate eSIM Lifecycle
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Microsoft Intune provides advanced hardware firmware and cellular connectivity lifecycle management for corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices (COBO, COSU, and COPE):

### 1. Samsung Knox E-FOTA Integration (July 2026 / 2607)
Admins can integrate **Samsung Knox E-FOTA (Firmware Over-The-Air)** directly in the Microsoft Intune admin center (included with **Microsoft 365 E3 / E5** and **Intune Plan 2**). This allows IT to:
- Lock and control the exact OS/firmware version deployed to corporate Samsung fleets.
- Force silent firmware updates without user interaction and schedule downloads/installations outside business hours to prevent frontline downtime.

### 2. Corporate Android eSIM Lifecycle Management (June–August 2026 / 2606–2608)
For corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices (Android 15+), Intune now supports end-to-end eSIM governance:
- **Expanded SIM Inventory:** View EIDs, multiple ICCIDs, and activation states under `Device details / Hardware`.
- **Remote Activate & Remove eSIM Actions:** Remotely activate an eSIM using a carrier activation code or remove an individual eSIM by ICCID from the single device view without wiping the device.
- **Wipe eSIM Preservation or Removal:** Choose whether to preserve or remove eSIMs during a single-device wipe, or enforce **Remove all eSIMs during a device wipe** via Settings Catalog policy.
- **Block Users from Adding eSIM Profiles:** Prevent unauthorized carrier profile additions via the Android Enterprise Settings Catalog.

## Implementation Guidance

1. Use the current Samsung enterprise update terminology and verify whether the organization is using Samsung E-FOTA, Knox-related licensing, or another supported Samsung update integration with Intune. Do not assume standard Android update policies give the same level of version control.
2. Build a firmware governance process that includes test devices, pilot users, and production rings. Samsung devices often vary by region, carrier, and model family, so validate each important hardware variant.
3. Document approved and blocked OS levels. Some business-critical apps or accessories may require a minimum patch level, while others may need a temporary hold until compatibility is confirmed.
4. Coordinate firmware waves with compliance policy and Conditional Access. If the organization requires a minimum Android security patch level, make sure the grace period and rollout timing are realistic for the chosen rings.
5. Plan user communications for reboots, battery requirements, and estimated downtime. Frontline devices should have charging, spare-device, or swap procedures during update windows.
6. Review update results after each wave and track failures by model, firmware build, carrier, and app bundle.

Tasks.Name: Specialty Devices (Android XR, visionOS & tvOS ADE)
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Microsoft Intune supports enterprise enrollment, configuration, app deployment, and compliance enforcement for spatial computing, AR/VR headsets, and shared display appliances—included with **Microsoft 365 E3 / E5** and **Microsoft Intune Plan 2** (Specialty Device Management).

Key 2026 platform additions include:
- **Android XR Device Management (April 2026):** Intune supports **Android XR** headsets and spatial devices using **Android Enterprise Dedicated (COSU)** and **Fully Managed (COBO)** enrollment modes. Admins can enroll Android XR devices, deploy apps via Managed Google Play, and enforce core security and compliance policies alongside standard Android devices.
- **Userless Apple Automated Device Enrollment (ADE) for visionOS and tvOS (April & July 2026 / 2604 & 2607):**
  - Supports **ADE without user affinity** for **Apple Vision Pro (visionOS 26+)** and **Apple TV (tvOS 26+)** through Apple Business Manager or Apple School Manager.
  - Includes **Setup Assistant screen skip controls** (such as *Apple ID*, *Diagnostics Data*, and *Location Services*) during ADE enrollment (2607).
  - Supports Settings Catalog policies, custom configuration profiles, default enrollment restrictions, and remote device actions under the **Apple mobile** filter in the Intune admin center.

## Implementation Guidance

1. Validate support by platform first. A mixed fleet might include HoloLens, Android-based immersive devices, or vendor-specific headsets. Do not build policy assumptions from one platform and apply them to another without checking Microsoft support documentation.
2. Define the user model: single user, shared user, kiosk, or technician device. This determines whether you need standard user enrollment, shared account handling, device-only usage, or line-of-business launcher experiences.
3. Lock down hardware capabilities to what the workflow requires. Review camera, microphone, Bluetooth, USB, browser access, local file storage, and sideloading behavior against the business need and privacy rules.
4. Package only approved apps and test update behavior carefully. AR/VR workflows are often sensitive to app latency, peripheral compatibility, and OS version changes.
5. Plan Wi-Fi, certificates, VPN or private access, and Conditional Access for the specific places these devices operate. Field and warehouse scenarios often fail because the network design was treated as an afterthought.
6. Monitor device health and have an operational replacement process. Specialized headsets usually need spare inventory and faster incident handling than knowledge-worker laptops.

## Reference

Tasks.Name: macOS Recovery Lock Management
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

On company-owned macOS devices (Apple silicon), **Recovery Lock** sets a firmware/recovery OS password that prevents users or attackers with physical access from booting the Mac into macOS Recovery mode, reinstalling macOS, accessing Terminal in recovery, or bypassing Automated Device Enrollment (ADE) remote management.

Introduced in **March 2026 (Service Release 2603)**, Microsoft Intune supports full lifecycle management of macOS Recovery Lock:
- **Settings Catalog Policy:** Enable the Recovery Lock feature and configure an automated **password rotation schedule**.
- **On-Demand Remote Device Action:** Trigger the **Rotate recovery lock password** remote action on any individual macOS device.
- **Audited Password Retrieval:** Authorized admins with the **Remote tasks/View macOS recovery lock password** RBAC permission can view the current Recovery Lock password in the per-setting status report (`Passwords and keys`).

This supports *Assume breach* and physical endpoint security on macOS, providing the Apple silicon equivalent of BIOS/UEFI password protection and pre-boot lockdown on Windows.

## Key Configuration Steps

1. In the Microsoft Intune admin center, create a **macOS Settings Catalog** policy (`Devices > Configuration > Create`).
2. Configure the **Recovery Lock** settings to enable Recovery Lock and define a regular password rotation schedule.
3. Grant the **Remote tasks/View macOS recovery lock password** Intune RBAC permission only to authorized helpdesk/security roles.
4. Use the **Rotate recovery lock password** remote action immediately after any recovery session where the password was disclosed to a user or technician.

## Reference

- [Rotate macOS recovery lock passcode in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/actions/rotate-recovery-lock-passcode)

Tasks.Name: Custom Compliance Policy (macOS)
Tasks.Doc:
## Overview

Introduced in **July 2026 (Service Release 2607)**, Microsoft Intune now supports **Custom Compliance settings for macOS**, bringing macOS to full parity with Windows and Linux custom compliance.

While built-in macOS compliance settings check standard attributes (FileVault, Firewall, Gatekeeper, OS version, and Defender risk score), **Custom Compliance** allows organizations to run a custom shell script via the Intune management agent for macOS and evaluate the returned JSON output against a custom JSON rules definition. This enables Zero Trust verification of:
- Third-party security agents (EDR, DLP, SASE/ZTNA daemons, certificate posture)
- Local macOS system hardening states (e.g., `sudo` configuration, SSH daemon status, TCC permissions, local AI agents)
- Custom hardware or file-integrity attributes

Results appear alongside standard compliance reporting in the Intune admin center and feed directly into **Microsoft Entra Conditional Access** device compliance evaluation.

## Key Configuration Steps

1. Write and test a macOS discovery shell script that outputs a flat JSON dictionary of key-value pairs to `stdout`.
2. Upload the discovery script in the Intune admin center under **Endpoint security > Device compliance > Scripts > Add > macOS**.
3. Create a JSON rules file defining the setting name, operator, data type, expected value, and remediation message for end users in Company Portal.
4. Create a **macOS Compliance Policy**, add the **Custom compliance** section, select your discovery script, and upload the JSON rules file.

## Reference

- [Use custom compliance settings in Microsoft Intune (Windows, Linux, and macOS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/compliance/custom-settings)
